name: Analog thumb joystick with select button
description: Analog 2-axis thumb joystick (PSP/Xbox style): two 10 kΩ potentiometers whose wipers output 0 V to Vcc (about Vcc/2 at rest) and a select switch that shorts Sel to GND when the stick is pressed. Runs on any supply up to 5 V (use 3.3 V with a 3.3 V board), about 1 mA at 5 V. Sold as: Adafruit Analog 2-axis Thumb Joystick with Select Button + Breakout Board (product 512), 5-pin header GND, Sel, Yout, Xout, Vcc.
eli5: A little thumb stick like on a game controller. It tells your board how far you push it left/right and up/down, and whether you click it down.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground for both pots and the select switch (header pin 1)

pins.name: Sel
pins.description: Select switch, shorts to GND while the stick is pressed; no pull-up on the board, use the GPIO's internal pull-up (pin 2)

pins.name: Yout
pins.description: Y-axis wiper voltage, 0 V to Vcc, about Vcc/2 at rest (pin 3)

pins.name: Xout
pins.description: X-axis wiper voltage, 0 V to Vcc, about Vcc/2 at rest (pin 4)

pins.name: Vcc
pins.description: Supply for both pots, up to 5 V (pin 5). With a 3.3 V board connect it to 3V3, or the outputs reach 5 V.

supplierQuery: Adafruit 512 analog 2-axis thumb joystick select button breakout
buildNotes: Header pin 1 is GND: GND, Sel, Yout, Xout, Vcc (read left to right on the silkscreen it is Vcc, Xout, Yout, Sel, GND).
The stick ships loose: solder it to the breakout, then solder the 5-pin header.
On an ESP32 or Pico connect Vcc to 3V3: the wipers swing all the way to the supply, and 5 V on an ADC pin can damage it.
Position (%) = 100 × Vout / Vcc; at rest each axis sits near 50 % (1.65 V at 3.3 V). Use a small dead zone.
Sel shorts to GND with no pull-up fitted: enable the GPIO's internal pull-up. It reads 0 while pressed.
On the ESP32 wire Xout and Yout to ADC1 pins (GPIO32-39); ADC2 stops working when Wi-Fi is on.

example.code:
from thumbjoystick import ThumbJoystick
import time

js = ThumbJoystick({XOUT}, {YOUT}, {SEL})
while True:
    print('X=%d Y=%d SEL=%d' % (round(js.x()), round(js.y()), js.pressed()))
    time.sleep(0.5)

test.title: Reports the stick position and select button set on the controls
